_readme: PROVISIONING settings for the combined TST/ACC environment (Test and Acceptance
are one environment for this feature — TAD ADR-006). The provisioning scripts take
-Env <dev|test|acc|prd>; `test` IS TST/ACC here and `acc` is never used, so this is
the file every `-Env test` call in config/revitalise-grant-automation-pipeline.yml
resolves to.
This is NOT the pac import settings file. Two different kinds of settings file live
in this folder and they are consumed by different tools:
• <env>-settings.json  (this file) — read by the PowerShell scripts in
provisioning/ via Get-ProvisioningSettings. Describes Entra groups, Dataverse
group teams, role bindings, auditing, retention jobs and setting rows.
• pac-import-tstacc.json / pac-import-prd.json — passed to
`pac solution import --settings-file`. Supplies environment variable VALUES and
connection reference bindings at solution import time. Nothing else.
Identifiers only — never a secret, token or connection string (C-TECH-001). The
provisioning app id and certificate thumbprint stay in the environment variables
named under 'auth' (CI secrets / Key Vault).
Every {{PLACEHOLDER}} must be replaced with the real per-environment value before
the pipeline runs: Get-Setting fails fast on any value that still contains {{...}}
(C-TECH-031 / C-TECH-047). Values that are POLICY rather than per-environment
(retention periods, audit retention days, the fixed scoring maps) are real values
here by design — they must be identical in every environment.

_comment_appRegistrations: App registrations are TENANT level, not per environment, so this block is IDENTICAL in
test-settings.json and prd-settings.json. That is deliberate and is the pattern
provisioning/README.md describes: run ensure-app-registration.ps1 once per settings file,
and idempotency makes the second run report EXISTS rather than creating a duplicate.
What IS per environment is the Dataverse application user, created by
PERMISSION IDS ARE {{PLACEHOLDER}} TOKENS ON PURPOSE, matching
dev-settings.example.json. The app-role GUIDs are stable across tenants but they are not
written here from memory: an incorrect GUID would grant a permission nobody reviewed.
Look each one up in the tenant (Graph: `GET /servicePrincipals(appId=...)?$select=appRoles`)
and paste it in. Every script fails fast while a token remains (C-TECH-047), so this
Least privilege is justified in TAD section 6.7 and ADR-018 (C-TECH-043):
Sites.Selected instead of Sites.FullControl.All, and Group.Create +
GroupMember.ReadWrite.All is tenant-wide and is the narrowest permission that can manage
group membership - which is why ADR-018 justifies it explicitly rather than assuming it.

appRegistrations._comment: THE TST/ACC DEPLOY IDENTITY, AND ONLY TST/ACC. Renamed and split from the former single shared `rev-grantautomation-deploy` on 2026-08-12 (ADR-007). Solution import/export and Power Platform Pipelines promotion into TST/ACC. Its authority in Dataverse comes from an APPLICATION USER IN TST/ACC ONLY, holding a least-privilege deployment role - NOT System Administrator, and not a broad API permission (TAD section 6.7). It must NOT be given an application user in PRD: that absence is the boundary.
appRegistrations._comment_why_split: Scoping several federated credentials onto ONE app registration would gate token ISSUANCE but not AUTHORITY - every subject would still resolve to a single service principal that is an application user in every environment, so a token minted by the tst_acc CI job could import into PRD. Splitting the registration moves the boundary to 'this identity does not exist in PRD at all', which is what C-TECH-043 least privilege asks for. Cost: this appRegistrations block is no longer identical to prd-settings.json - see config/revitalise-grant-automation-pipeline.yml tenant_prerequisites.

This is the tenant-wide Dataverse service-principal scope id, so the identical value applies to every place this permission is declared in this file (also appRegistrations[1]'s Dataverse block below).

federatedCredentials._comment: C-TECH-044 RESOLVED 2026-08-12 - this credential is now the one actually in use, and no client secret exists on this registration. .github/workflows/ci.yml authenticates with `pac auth create --githubFederated`, which needs only the application id and tenant id.
federatedCredentials._comment_subject: THE SUBJECT IS THE GITHUB ENVIRONMENT, NOT A BRANCH. GitHub's OIDC `sub` claim is `repo:ORG/REPO:environment:NAME` for any job that references an environment, and only `repo:ORG/REPO:ref:refs/heads/BRANCH` for one that does not (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/oidc). Entra matches subjects as EXACT STRINGS with no wildcards. The previous value here was `ref:refs/heads/main`, which would never have matched: this workflow triggers on `feature/**`, so a branch subject would need one credential per branch name. Every authenticating job in ci.yml therefore declares an `environment:`, giving this one fixed subject per identity. EXACTLY ONE credential belongs on this registration - adding a second subject here would re-open the hole that splitting the registrations closed.
federatedCredentials.name: github-actions-env-tst-acc
federatedCredentials._comment_subject_resolved: RESOLVED 2026-08-21 from ground truth, not from memory: `git remote -v` in this repository returns https://github.com/Argelis-XVL/Revitalise.git, so the org is Argelis-XVL and the repo is Revitalise; the environment segment is `tst_acc`, the GitHub Environment name .github/workflows/ci.yml actually declares. Entra matches this subject as an exact string with no wildcards, so if the repository is ever renamed or transferred this value must be re-read from the remote and re-pasted — a stale subject fails token exchange with an authentication error that names nothing (IMP-0175).
federatedCredentials.subject: repo:Argelis-XVL/Revitalise:environment:tst_acc

As of 2026-08-14 the reviewer confirmed they cannot grant admin consent for Microsoft Graph application permissions on this tenant (role limitation, not a preference), so the Group.Create / GroupMember.ReadWrite.All permission block that used to sit here was REMOVED rather than left unconsentable and unused (least privilege, C-TECH-043 — don't request a permission nothing exercises). If a later phase needs scripted group creation after all, the permission block that was here is preserved in git history (see the commit that removed it) rather than re-derived from memory.
appRegistrations._comment_dataverse: The Dataverse permission below is what this registration is actually used for now: ensure-schema.ps1 (provisioning/dataverse/) authenticates with this SAME PROVISION_APP_ID/PROVISION_CERT_THUMBPRINT credential to call the Dataverse Web API metadata endpoints. Mirrors the Dataverse permission block already declared on the rev-grantautomation-deploy-* registrations below: 'Dynamics CRM' only ever exposes ONE permission, user_impersonation, shown as a Delegated Scope in the Entra portal even when it backs an app-only client-credentials grant — there is no separate Application-type Dataverse permission to request. Consenting this scope is necessary but not sufficient: the app ALSO needs a Dataverse Application User in the target environment with a role capable of metadata operations (System Administrator or System Customizer — not a plain custom role, since CreateEntityRequest/CreateAttributeRequest-equivalent Web API calls aren't covered by the custom-privilege model at all). CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-08-14: live WhoAmI call against DEV succeeded once the application user was added there.

ALEX'S WORDPRESS SITE AS AN OAUTH CLIENT-CREDENTIALS CALLER, and the identity the PRIMARY authentication control on the intake endpoint is built around (NFR-008, C-TECH-006). Created by provisioning/entra/ensure-intake-client.ps1, which also PRINTS the two identifiers the control needs: the application (client) id goes into the rev_IntakeAllowedClientId environment variable (the flow's second gate) and the SERVICE PRINCIPAL OBJECT ID goes into the trigger's 'Allowed users' field (the platform-level primary gate). They are different values and are not interchangeable.
appRegistrations._comment_adr011: ADR-011 IS RE-DECIDED (TAD rev 14, 2026-10-02): trigger mode Anyone (the signed callback URL) plus the x-rev-client-id header. This registration is KEPT only because its application (client) id is the value the website sends as x-rev-client-id. Its client secret, given to Alex on 2026-09-25, is no longer needed by anything; revoking it is a reviewer/Wanstor action. SUPERSEDED (rev 10, retained): ADR-011 IS DECIDED (TAD rev 10, 2026-09-25): the Entra client-credentials route - this registration - on the reviewer's statement 'I have shared the url, clientid and secret with Alex'. The shared-secret and scheduled REST-pull routes are dead options, so their teardown instruction that stood here is retired (ADR-011 consequence 4). The caller's client secret lives in WordPress, outside our secret store: it needs a named rotation owner and a recorded expiry (C-TECH-044, SOFT, <= 180 days); a certificate stays preferred. When it expires every submission gets a 401 at the platform gate and the flow never runs (risk A-R68). ensure-intake-client.ps1 reports the credential count; verify-intake-endpoint-auth.ps1 is the per-environment check.

A pipeline that mints a credential is a pipeline that prints one (C-TECH-001). ensure-intake-client.ps1 reports whether one exists, by COUNT only.

Resolve both values in the tenant: `GET /servicePrincipals?$filter=displayName eq 'Microsoft Flow Service'&$select=appId,oauth2PermissionScopes`. The appId is commonly published as 7df0a125-d3be-4c96-aa54-591f83ff541c - CONFIRM that against the tenant rather than trusting it, then paste. The scope to take is the one named `User`.

resourceAccess._comment: Permission: User (delegated Scope) on Microsoft Flow Service. ⚠ ONE ITEM TO CONFIRM ON FIRST RUN: every published walkthrough of this pattern declares the DELEGATED `User` scope and then acquires an APP-ONLY token with `.default`, which is an unusual combination. If Entra refuses the client-credentials request, the fix is to grant the equivalent APPLICATION permission on the same resource and change `type` here to `Role`. Recorded rather than assumed - do not discover this in PRD.

intake._comment_endpointUrl: THE TRIGGER URL IS A CREDENTIAL AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT A VALUE IN THIS FILE. A Power Automate HTTP trigger URL carries its own SAS signature in the `sig=` query parameter — Microsoft documents regenerating it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/regenerate-sas-key), which is only meaningful for a secret. It is held as a CI secret under this name, like PROVISION_APP_ID (C-TECH-001/047). Read it once from the trigger card after the flow is turned on.

auditing._comment: 6 years = 2192 days (C-DOM-010, C-DOM-011, TAD §6.5). A longer period — and -1, retain forever — would keep applicant data in audit history after the record itself was deleted, so this number is reviewed with the DPO, not defaulted in code.
auditing._comment_auditedTables: Every table under src/solutions/*/Entities/ must appear here — asserted by scripts/verify-audited-tables.py (build gate `audited-tables`, C-TECH-064's source-side half). rev_grant and rev_review were added 2026-08-22 (IMP-0178): rev_review shipped in Phase 3 task 6.4 with no audit trail in DEV, and IMP-0085 had predicted exactly that for each of the five tables still to be built. Table-level auditing is entity METADATA that no solution import can set or clear (IMP-0086), so a table absent from this list is a table nobody switches on.

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Paid Grant Applications
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applications at Grant Paid once the grant's rev_finalpaymentdate is older than 72 months (6 years); the cascade removes Review, Grant and Payment (C-DOM-003, ADR-004, ADR-083).

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Rejected Applications
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applications with status Rejected once rev_decisiondate is older than 12 months (C-DOM-003, ADR-004).

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Withdrawn or Incomplete Applications
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applications with status Withdrawn or Incomplete once the parent applicant's rev_lastcontactdate is older than 6 months (C-DOM-003, ADR-004).

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Orphaned Applicants
bulkDeleteJobs._comment: No retention period of its own: an applicant with no remaining application inherits the period of whichever job deleted the last child. Runs after the two application sweeps (TAD §3.4 gap 1).
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applicant records that have no remaining child application — the derived orphan sweep.

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Error Log
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes error log rows once rev_occurredon is older than 90 days. Error rows contain no personal data (C-DOM-004).

settingRows.description: Sets how many circumstance points each answer to the ten wellbeing questions is worth. Used by the scoring process for every application. The keys are the answer positions 1 to 6 as listed on the form: 1 is the first answer ('None of the time' or 'Strongly disagree'), 5 is the fifth ('All of the time' or 'Strongly agree'), 6 is 'Not sure'. Position 1 scores 5 points and position 5 scores 1, because all ten questions are worded so that a frequent occurrence or an agreement means better wellbeing and so less need. 'Not sure' scores 0, so it adds nothing. One map serves both answer scales because they share the same six positions. Use whole numbers or halves only: any other fraction breaks the rounding of the final score. It must stay valid JSON with a key for every position 1 to 6; if the row is missing or broken, scoring stops and raises an alert. Changing a value changes the maximum possible score, so check MaxCircumstanceScore too.

Turns the life-satisfaction answer (0 to 10) into circumstance points so that lower satisfaction scores more. Used by the scoring process for every application. The keys are the answers 0 to 10 and each value is the points for that answer; as supplied, an answer of 0 scores 10 points, 5 scores 5 and 10 scores 0 (10 minus the answer). It is a lookup table rather than a calculation so the direction of the scale can be changed here without changing the scoring process. It needs an entry for every whole number from 0 to 10 and must stay valid JSON; if the row is missing or broken, scoring stops and raises an alert. If you change the highest value, update MaxCircumstanceScore to match.

The circumstance score at or below which an application is automatically rejected. Used by the scoring process: after it works out the score, an application scoring this number or lower gets the status Auto-reject, whatever else is true, and the reason is recorded on the application. This check is made before the borderline band, so an application at or below this number can never end up as Borderline. Enter a whole number, for example 20. Keep it below the lower end of the borderline band. If the row is missing or not a whole number, scoring stops and raises an alert, so no application is scored until it is fixed. A change applies to applications scored from then on; applications already scored are not re-scored.

The lowest circumstance score that counts as Borderline, meaning the application needs the process owner's judgement. Used by the scoring process: a score from this number up to and including BorderlineBandUpper gives the status Borderline and sends the process owner a Teams message with a link to the application. Enter a whole number, for example 21. Keep it above KnockoutThreshold; a score at or below KnockoutThreshold is rejected before this band is considered. If the row is missing or not a whole number, scoring stops and raises an alert. A change applies to applications scored from then on; applications already scored are not re-scored.

The highest circumstance score that still counts as Borderline. Used by the scoring process: a score from BorderlineBandLower up to and including this number gives the status Borderline for the process owner's judgement, and a score above it gives Auto-pass. Enter a whole number, for example 30, not lower than BorderlineBandLower. If the row is missing or not a whole number, scoring stops and raises an alert. A change applies to applications scored from then on; applications already scored are not re-scored.

The highest annual household income, in pounds, that is still eligible. Used by the scoring process: it takes the top of the income band the applicant chose on the form (see IncomeBandUpperBoundMap) and compares it with this figure. If the top of the band is at or below this figure the income check passes; if it is above, the application is automatically rejected as above the income ceiling. Applicants who say they receive means-tested benefits are never rejected on income, and an application with no income band is not rejected for income. Enter the amount in pounds as a plain number, for example 25000. If the row is missing or not a number, scoring stops and raises an alert. Remember that income bands are compared by their upper limit, so the ceiling should normally match the top of one of the bands.

The smallest number of applications needed before an average money figure is shown to trustees. Used by the round statistics process behind the trustee landing screen. In the table by type of break, the average cost, the average grant requested and the grant share for a row are shown only when at least this many applications in that row carry a figure; otherwise the cell is left blank and only the number of applications is shown. This protects individual applicants from being identified in small groups, so treat it as a privacy safeguard and not a tuning knob. Enter a whole number, digits only, for example 5. If the row is missing, empty or not digits, all these money figures are withheld.

How long, in seconds, the round figures on the trustee landing screen count as current. Used by the trustee screen and the round statistics process: figures worked out within this time are shown at once, while older figures are recalculated when a trustee opens the screen or uses Refresh figures. Several trustees opening the screen in the same few minutes therefore cause only one calculation. Enter a whole number, digits only; 300 is five minutes. If the row is missing or not digits, figures are never treated as current and are recalculated every time the screen opens, which is slower but never shows out-of-date figures.

Used by the round statistics process: it counts the applications received in each month from this date to the present. Enter the date as year-month-day, for example 2026-02-16. A wrong date silently moves every month's boundary and so every month's count, so check it before changing it. If the row is missing, the month-by-month history is simply not shown.

settingRows.displayName: Round statistics: applications received before tracking start
settingRows.description: The number of applications received before the monthly counting began (see RoundStatisticsHistoryStartDate). Used by the trustee screen: it is added to this round's count to show how many applications there have been in total and this round's share of them. Enter a whole number, digits only. 0 is a real value meaning none before then, not a blank. If the row is missing while the start date is set, the total is flagged as understated and the screen shows 'All applications' as not recorded instead of a share.

How far, as a percentage, a month's application count can differ from the average of the previous six months before it is flagged as unusual. Used by the round statistics process for the month-by-month counts shown to trustees. With 50, a month more than 50 percent above or below its six-month average is flagged. If the previous six months averaged zero, any application in the month is flagged. A month with fewer than six months of history behind it is never flagged. Enter a whole number, digits only. If the row is missing, no month is flagged. A wrong value only changes which months are flagged and can be corrected at any time.

How many days an acceptance agreement may stay unsigned before the process owner is told. Used by the daily acceptance reminders and escalation process: it looks for grants whose agreement was sent at least this many days ago and is still not signed, and sends the process owner a Teams message with the applicant's details. Each grant is escalated only once. Enter a whole number of days, for example 14. If the row is missing the process uses 14. If it holds something that is not a whole number the process fails and raises an alert.

When DocuSign sends automatic reminders for an unsigned acceptance agreement. Used by the acceptance process when it sends an agreement: it asks DocuSign to remind the signers on these days. Enter two whole numbers in square brackets, first and second reminder day counted from sending, for example [3,7]. DocuSign can only be told the day of the first reminder and the gap between reminders, so after the first reminder (day 3) further reminders repeat at the same gap as between the two numbers (every 4 days) until the agreement is signed or expires. If the row is missing the process uses [3,7]. The second number must be larger than the first. If the row is not two numbers in this form, the sending run fails and raises an alert.

settingRows.description: The list of gendered and family words the narrative scrubbing replaces with neutral ones. Used by the scrubbing process, which rewrites an applicant's free-text answers to remove personal details before trustees see them. Write one entry per line as 'word = neutral word', for example 'mum = parent'. Where the sentence decides which word fits, write 'word = first or second'. The words on the left are rewritten by the AI and then checked afterwards: any of them still in the text sends the record for review. The words on the right are the only neutral words the rewrite may use. A neutral word must not also appear on the left. If the row is missing, empty or has a line that is not 'word = word', no narratives are scrubbed until it is fixed. Use made-up examples only: never paste text from an application into this row.

settingRows.value:

settingRows.description: The titles the narrative scrubbing removes from free-text answers. Used by the scrubbing process: the rewrite removes these titles, and afterwards the text is checked and sent for review if one is still there. Write one title per line, 1 to 10 letters with an optional full stop, for example Mr or Dr. The check matches capital letters as written (Ms Smith, not MS). Write 'none' if no titles should be removed. If the row is missing or empty, or a line is not a valid title, no narratives are scrubbed until it is fixed. Use made-up examples only: never paste text from an application into this row.

settingRows.displayName: Narrative scrubbing - how names are handled
settingRows.value:
When [NAME] is the writer's own name, keep [NAME]. This includes "I am [NAME]", "I'm [NAME]", "my name is [NAME]" and any sentence where the writer says [NAME] is what they are called, such as "[NAME] is the name my friends use for me".
Keep [NAME] after Dr: "Dr [NAME] reviews my medication" stays as it is.
When [NAME] comes straight after a relationship word, remove it and keep the neutral word, even when the text names other people: "my husband [NAME]" becomes "my partner", and "our son [NAME], who is [AGE 35 to 44]," becomes "our child, who is [AGE 35 to 44],".
Otherwise, keep [NAME] when the text names two or more different people other than the writer.
If the text is about one named person, write they, them or their in place of [NAME], as the sentence needs, and make the verb agree: "[NAME] visits me." becomes "They visit me."
A name inside the name of a GP practice is part of [GP PRACTICE].
Mum or Dad used as a name, as in "Mum helps me", becomes "my parent".
settingRows.description: Plain-language rules telling the narrative rewrite how to handle names. Used by the scrubbing process, which replaces each name with the label [NAME] and then follows these rules about when to keep or remove it, for example keep [NAME] when it is the writer's own name, and remove it after a relationship word such as 'my husband [NAME]'. Write one rule per line in plain words. The rules guide the rewrite only; they are not checked afterwards. If the row is missing or empty, no narratives are scrubbed until it is fixed. Use made-up examples only: never paste text from an application into this row.

settingRows.displayName: Narrative scrubbing - labels the rewrite may write
settingRows.value:
[NAME] = a person's name
[ADDRESS] = a street, a house name or number, a town in an address, or a postcode
[PHONE] = a phone number
[EMAIL] = an email address
[GP PRACTICE] = the name of a GP practice or surgery
settingRows.description: The labels the narrative rewrite is allowed to write in place of personal details. Used by the scrubbing process: it replaces personal details with these labels, for example [NAME] or [PHONE], and any other label it writes fails the check and sends the record for review. Write one per line as '[LABEL] = what it covers', with the label in capitals in square brackets, for example '[PHONE] = a phone number'. If the row is missing, empty or has a line in the wrong shape, no narratives are scrubbed until it is fixed. Use made-up examples only: never paste text from an application into this row.

settingRows.displayName: Narrative scrubbing - confidence threshold for the review hint
settingRows.description: The confidence level below which a scrubbed narrative is marked to look at more carefully. Used by the scrubbing process: when the lowest confidence the AI reported for any detail in an application is below this number, the process owner's card carries the hint 'below-threshold'. It is only a hint. Nothing is released automatically: you review and release every scrubbed application yourself. 0.85, 85 and 85% all mean 85 percent. If the row is missing or not a number between 0 and 100, the card shows the hint 'threshold-missing-or-invalid' instead. The row is set once when it is first created; after that it is yours to adjust in the app and a release never overwrites it.

settingRows.description: Switches on or off the rule that rejects applicants with savings over 6,000 pounds. Used by the scoring process: while it is true, an application where the applicant answered Yes to having savings over 6,000 pounds is automatically rejected as Auto-reject, whatever its score, and the reason is recorded. While it is false the answer is ignored. A blank answer never rejects. Enter true or false and nothing else: any other value stops scoring with an alert, so a typing slip cannot silently switch the rule off. You edit this value in the app and a release never overwrites it.

While it is false the answers are ignored. A blank answer never rejects. Enter true or false and nothing else: any other value stops scoring with an alert, so a typing slip cannot silently switch the rule off. You edit this value in the app and a release never overwrites it.

apps._comment_finance: REV Finance ADDED wbs:8.2, TAD §6.2.1 deliverable #7 / ADR-048 (rev 6). Not a separate app — the payment-capture area (wbs:8.3) lives inside this existing REV Grant Administration app. This is a NAVIGATION boundary, not a security one: the barrier keeping Applicant/Application/Review/Setting off this persona's screen is the role's own table privileges (Roles/REV Finance/REV Finance.xml — no privilege on any of those tables), not the app's role list.

_comment_trusteeCodeAppAbsent: The trustee Code App (WBS 6.1) is intentionally absent from dataverse.apps[] even
though WBS 6.5 is active. It is added only after a real `pac code push` has assigned
an appId: running `share-apps.ps1 -Env test` with a {{TRUSTEE_CODE_APP_ID}} placeholder
would cause a post_deploy step (which is live and wired for TST/ACC) to throw at
Get-Setting time, failing a deploy that works today. Assumption A-TR-3 in
share-apps.ps1 forbids inventing a platform-assigned id (C-TECH-051). The two-step
closure sequence — first publish the app to assign an id, then add the entry — is in
block. That ordering guarantees the id is real before it is configured.

_comment_omitted_blocks: No `sharepoint` and no `teams` block, deliberately. Phase 1 provisions no
SharePoint site (the four tables hold no documents — DocuSign and file storage are
later phases) and no Microsoft Team: the only Teams usage is a 1:1 chat
notification sent to the process owner through the Teams connector (TAD ADR-015),
which needs a connection reference in pac-import-tstacc.json, not a provisioned
team. There is also no `code` app entry — Phase 1 ships the model-driven app only.
The pipeline therefore calls no sharepoint/* or teams/* script.
